battle.name: 巴比倫帝國的衰弱與滅亡
battle.theater: 幼發拉底河中游與安納托利亞高原
battle.brief: 編年列表裡的一段總目，下分加喜特人入侵巴比倫、巴比倫進攻「海地王朝」（實為赫梯）與巴比倫的洗劫（前1595）三節。王朝在宮廷內鬥與赫梯南下的夾擊下崩解，城市易主而制度延續。卡面的埃及長矛屬早王朝銅矛工藝，正是這批近東軍隊手中青銅長矛的祖型；勝負其實由戰車與攻城槌決定。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 「巴比倫帝國的衰弱與滅亡」在編年列表裡不是一場會戰，而是一段跨度一百五十年的總目，其下分列三節：公元前1740年的加喜特人入侵巴比倫、公元前1700年的巴比倫進攻「海地王朝」、公元前1595年的巴比倫的洗劫；同一段裡還有「海地王朝的建立」（公元前1732年），即安納托利亞的赫梯建國。第一節的交戰方是幼發拉底河中游的巴比倫城邦與自敘利亞、巴勒斯坦方向南下的西閃米特武裝集團加喜特人；第二節是巴比倫對安納托利亞高原的赫梯，條目所記的「海地」是「赫梯」轉錄之訛；第三節則是赫梯王穆爾西里一世攻入巴比倫城。巴比倫方的指揮系統是王庭與神廟的雙軌：宮廷領土與城郊各區按丁口徵發步兵，盟屬城邦供應戰車與弓手，埃薩吉拉與埃特曼安基兩座神廟握有穀物、銅料與雇傭兵的實權，而王位繼承本身就是宮廷鬥爭的結果。赫梯方的編制更老練：以哈圖沙為核心，王室直屬的步兵與個人乘騎的戰車隊是骨架，各附庸小國按約提供兵員，軍隊每年越過幼發拉底河作季節性遠征。加喜特人自成一體，是以戰車貴族為首、以弓手與投槍手為群的軍事集團，奪權之後沿用巴比倫的書吏與文書，以蘇美爾—阿卡德語繼續記錄城務；埃蘭的軍隊在東面虎視，亞述在北面趁勢坐大，阿拉美與埃什南納則先後脫離巴比倫的體系。
countriesEn: The fall of the Babylonian empire is not a battle in the war list but a heading covering a span of a hundred and fifty years, and three entries sit under it: the Kassite invasion of Babylon in 1740 BC, Babylon's attack on the so-called Haitian dynasty in 1700 BC, and the sack of Babylon in 1595 BC; in the same stretch stands the establishment of the Haitian dynasty, 1732 BC, which is the founding of the Hittite state in Anatolia. In the first entry the opponents are the city-state of Babylon on the middle Euphrates and a West Semitic armed group, the Kassites, moving south from the direction of Syria and Palestine. In the second, Babylon faces the Hittites of the Anatolian plateau, the name Haiti in the list being a scribal corruption of Hatti. In the third, the Hittite king Mursili I enters the city of Babylon. The Babylonian command system was a dual track of palace and temple: the royal demes and the districts around the city levied infantry by headcount, the client towns furnished chariots and archers, and the two great shrines, Esagila and the ziggurat Etemenanki, held the grain, the copper and the mercenaries in their own hands, while the succession to the throne was itself the outcome of palace quarrels. The Hittite organisation was the more disciplined of the two: Hattusa at the centre, the king's own infantry and his personal chariot corps as the skeleton, client principalities providing contingents by treaty, and the army crossing the Euphrates every year on a campaigning season. The Kassites formed a separate body, a military group led by chariot lords and followed by bowmen and javelin-throwers; once in control they kept the Babylonian scribes and the documents, and continued to record the city's business in Sumero-Akkadian. The army of Elam watched from the east, Assyria grew stronger in the north, and Yamhad and Eshnunna dropped out of the Babylonian system one after another.
people: 這段歷史留下的人名分屬兩個時代。巴比倫一側最關鍵的是漢摩拉比本人：在位約二十年的跨度裡，他把阿摩利特人散居的城邦拼成一個帝國，摧毀馬里、吞併埃什南納，並把秩序刻在玄武岩石柱上；他在位第四十六年被人暗殺，暗殺者很可能就是他的兒子薩姆舒迪塔那，帝國也從那一刻起碎裂。薩姆舒迪塔那、阿比-伊沙圖、尼努爾塔-阿普拉、伊布尼-阿普拉四位繼承者沒有一個守得住北疆，最後一位伊布尼-阿普拉死在攻打哈蘭的圍城之中，他之後的烏什希只在泥板上留下名字。亞述的沙姆希-阿達德一世約在公元前1775年入主巴比倫，把王宮搬到幼發拉底河中游，卻在漢摩拉比的攻勢下退出；他的孫子伊什梅達甘一世在北方接續強勢，替巴比倫的衰敗騰出空間。赫梯方面，赫梯國的建立者阿尼塔在十七世紀初已把哈蘇瓦與阿拉拉赫夷平，並把當地人口整批遷往哈圖沙；其子哈圖西里一世在位時攻下馬里與哈蘭，其孫穆爾西里一世率軍入巴比倫城，是列表「巴比倫的洗劫」那一節的主角。加喜特（卡西特）一方留下的是王的姓名與王表，而不是將領姓名，這本身就說明那一節的交接不是靠會戰完成的。文本層面的關鍵人物是公元前三世紀的埃及祭司史家馬涅托，他記錄的加喜特人統治巴比倫尼亞數百年之說，經由約瑟夫斯與歐伊修斯轉述，是今日加喜特說法的源頭，也是必須被批判的對象；在他寫作之前很久，埃克胡爾的泥板裡連續出現過卡西特王的姓名。考古層面的兩位功臣是二十世紀初在蘇薩發現《漢摩拉比法典》石柱的雅克・德・摩根，以及用應力裂痕證實公元前十七世紀中葉那場大火的霍莉・皮特曼與埃莉諾・巴利。
peopleEn: The names that survive from this stretch belong to two different eras. The most important on the Babylonian side is Hammurabi himself: in a reign of about twenty years he assembled the scattered Amorite city-states into an empire, destroyed Mari, absorbed Eshnunna and fixed the order of that empire on a basalt stele. He was assassinated in the forty-sixth year of his reign, very probably by his own son Samsu-ditana, and the empire began to come apart at that moment. Samsu-ditana, Abbi-shattu, Ninurta-apla and Ibni-apla, his four successors, held none of the northern frontier; the last of them, Ibni-apla, died in the siege of Harran, and his successor Ushshi survives only as a name on a tablet. Shamshi-Adad I of Assyria occupied Babylon around 1775 BC and moved the court there to the middle Euphrates, only to be driven out by Hammurabi's offensive; his grandson Ishme-Dagan I kept Assyria strong in the north, which left the room that Babylon's decline required. On the Hittite side, Anitta, the founder of the Hittite state, had already levelled Hassuwa and Alalakh in the early seventeenth century and moved their populations wholesale to Hattusa; his son Hattusili I took Mari and Harran, and his grandson Mursili I marched into Babylon, the protagonist of the list's sack of Babylon. On the Kassite side what survives is a list of royal names rather than a list of generals, which itself shows that that section of the story was a handover completed without a set-piece battle. The decisive personality on the level of texts is the third-century BC Egyptian priest-historian Manetho, whose account of the Kassite rule over Babylonia was transmitted by Josephus and Eusebius, and who is the source of the modern Hyksos story and also the thing that has to be criticised. Long before he wrote, the tablets of Ekur already carried the names of Kassite kings in unbroken sequence. On the level of archaeology two names count: Jacques de Morgan, who found the stele of the Code of Hammurabi at Susa in the early twentieth century, and Holly Pittman and Eleanor Barley, who used stress fractures to establish the conflagration of the mid-seventeenth century BC.
kits: 兵器卡上的埃及長矛是這段戰爭裡最不起眼、卻貫穿全程的底層裝備。早王朝時期的埃及人把燧石或銅、砷銅矛頭以纏繩與套箍固定在直木杆上，杆長多在兩米上下，無血槽，杆尾可加配重或銅箍；同時期王墓畫面與權杖頭圖樣已把持矛的護衛列入編制，說明矛在城垣與儀仗中屬制式裝備。到巴比倫第一王朝末年，這門技術在兩河流域與安納托利亞都已成熟為套筒青銅矛頭接硬木杆的樣式，矛成為雙方步兵的骨幹：赫梯的散兵列成密陣，以盾牌互相搭接形成連續正面，身前是長矛，側面配銅盔、短劍與手斧，弓手用複合反曲弓；巴比倫的近戰主力除矛兵外，靠大型四馬重車作機動核心，早期重輪大車同時是搬運城牆石料與木材的運輸車。加喜特與埃蘭的步兵同樣以矛、投槍與短柄斧為主，並配複合弓與銅箭鏃；攻城一方靠撞槌（槌頭初包銅，後以青銅條與木材合釘）、投石與牆基地道，守方則以石壘與泥磚段、箭雨與滾木消耗進攻者的體力。運輸端依賴牛群、驢隊與河船：銅料自上幼發拉底河與安納托利亞方向沿商路運入，錫則走更遠的陸路，銅錫合金的出現讓矛頭比早王朝的純銅更耐折。卡面這件早王朝標本在這段歷史上的位置因此很清楚：它是第一代金屬矛的代表，是往後兩百年間被不斷改寫的那一類工具的起點，而不是任何一次決定勝負的武器。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card is the least conspicuous and the most continuous piece of equipment in this war. In the Early Dynastic period the Egyptians lashed flint or copper and arsenical-copper heads to straight wooden shafts with cord and ferrule, the shafts running close to two metres, without a fuller, and sometimes carrying a counterweight or a copper butt-cap; the royal tomb scenes and the decorated maceheads of the same age already list spearmen among the escort, which shows the spear to be standard kit for walls and ceremony. By the end of the Babylonian First Dynasty the craft had matured in Mesopotamia and Anatolia into the socketed bronze head fitted to a hard wooden shaft, and the spear had become the backbone of the infantry on both sides: the Hittite loose troops closed into dense ranks whose overlapping shields formed a continuous face, with the spear in front, bronze helmets, short swords and hand axes at the side, and composite recurve bows for the archers; on the Babylonian side the close-combat force was the spearmen plus the heavy four-horse chariot as the mobile core, the early solid-wheeled car serving equally to haul wall stone and timber. The infantry of the Kassites and of Elam fought with spear, javelin and short-handled axe, and carried the composite bow with copper-tipped arrows. The attacker used battering rams, whose heads were first sheathed in copper and later built of bronze strips riveted to timber, together with stone-throwers and tunnels driven under the foundations, while the defenders answered with stone revetments and mud-brick sections, with arrow-falls and falling timbers to wear down the assault. Transport depended on oxen, donkey trains and river boats. Copper came down from the upper Euphrates and from Anatolia along the caravan roads, tin came by a much longer road, and the arrival of copper-tin alloy made spearheads tougher to break than the pure copper of the Early Dynastic age. The position of the Early Dynastic specimen on the card in this stretch of history is therefore clear: it is the type of the first generation of metal spears, the starting point of a class of tool that was rewritten again and again over the two centuries that followed, and not the weapon that decided any single outcome.
tactics: 這段衰落的軍事過程可以拆成三種不同的樣子。巴比倫帝國瓦解的第一階段是保衛戰：王朝末期沒有可靠的常備兵，守方靠城牆、水渠與分段駐防的民兵，把城外的耕地、牧場與道路視為必須守住的東西；敵軍往往不必攻城，只要奪走渡口、驛站並切斷河道，城堡就會在缺少穀物與柴薪的情況下自行癱瘓。進入加喜特（卡西特）統治之後，戰爭性質變成接管而非會戰：新統治者保留原有的書吏、神廟與度量衡，以既成事實換掉王朝，把神廟倉庫、泥板檔案與河運船隻握在自己手裡，這是西亞常見的干涉模式。赫梯方的戰法則是季節性遠征：開春後隊伍越過幼發拉底河，先以輕型雙馬戰車在陣前驅散敵軍，再以長矛密陣與大盾列城正面壓上，攻城時集中撞槌攻門與城牆的弱段，並在牆基掘進地道；破城之後的國家機器運作包含把居民整批遷往安納托利亞的高地，以切斷被征服者在原地的人事與土地結構，並把神像與石刻運回哈圖沙。巴比倫方在遠征時的弱點，正在於深入之後回程的補給線被切斷，這正是《巴比倫編年史》殘片所記的失敗型態。而真正改變整個區域權力結構的，是戰車這種以速度換取戰略主動的裝備：一旦有了馬匹與輕車，遊牧式的軍事集團就能脫離城牆的保護，直接在河谷裡往復打擊，帝國的防禦縱深因此失去意義。
tacticsEn: The military process of this decline can be split into three different shapes. The first stage of the collapse of the Babylonian empire was a war of defence: the late dynasty had no reliable standing army, and the defence rested on walls, canals and militia holding stretches of the perimeter, treating the fields, the pastures and the roads outside the city as things that had to be held. The enemy often did not need to assault at all; taking the fords, the staging posts and cutting the river was enough, and the citadel would falter for want of grain and firewood. Once the Kassites were in control, the character of the contest changed from battle to takeover: the new rulers kept the existing scribes, the shrines and the weights and measures, replaced the dynasty by accomplished fact, and put their hands on the temple storehouses, the tablet archives and the river boats, which is the standard West Asian pattern of intervention. Hittite method was the campaigning season: the columns crossed the Euphrates after the spring opening, light two-horse chariots disorganised the enemy in front of the line, dense spear ranks with large overlapping shields pressed the attack home, the rams were concentrated on the gates and the weaker stretches of the curtain, and tunnels were driven under the foundations. Once a city was taken, the machinery of the state included moving the population wholesale up into the Anatolian highlands, so as to break up the personnel and land structures of the conquered, and carrying the gods and the inscribed stones back to Hattusa. The weakness of the Babylonian expeditions lay in the line of supply being cut on the way home after the army had gone deep, and that is precisely the pattern of failure recorded in the fragments of the Babylonian Chronicle. What truly changed the balance of power in the region was the chariot, the piece of equipment that buys strategic initiative with speed. Once horses and light cars existed, a nomadic-style armed group could leave the protection of walls altogether and strike up and down the valley, and the defensive depth of an empire lost its meaning.
data: 先把年代表說清楚。漢摩拉比的統治年代通行作公元前1792年至前1750年；馬里在公元前1760年被漢摩拉比摧毀，馬里王宮的文書庫自1933年起由法國考古隊發掘，出土泥板以萬計；沙姆希-阿達德一世約在公元前1775年一度占領巴比倫；赫梯王阿尼塔在十七世紀初夷平哈蘇瓦與阿拉拉赫，哈圖西里一世在位約公元前1650年至前1620年，其子穆爾西里一世入巴比倫城的年份，現代通行作公元前1595年。列表所用的公元前1740年出自舊紀年：依《巴比倫王表甲》把加喜特（卡西特）統治折算為數百年、並由王朝更替往前推的算法，加喜特奪取巴比倫在舊說中定於公元前1740年，學界早於二十世紀中期已把這一系年代下修一百五十年上下，因此同一份列表裡的1740與1700屬舊紀年，而1595屬新紀年，兩者並不同源。城市規模方面，舊巴比倫時期的巴比倫城面積不足一百公頃，外牆由辛穆巴里特一世主持營建，環城周長以公里計，城內神廟群與泥板檔案以萬計。一九〇一年至一九〇二年，雅克・德・摩根在蘇薩的發掘中挖出《漢摩拉比法典》石柱；該柱在公元前1595年被帶離巴比倫，現藏巴黎羅浮宮，這是這場戰爭留下的最具體的單一物證。卡西特王朝在巴比倫尼亞的統治長度，文獻給出的數字是四百二十六年，該王朝終結於公元前1155年前後埃蘭王舒特魯克納胡恩特洗劫巴比倫。月份欄填四月，是依美索不達米亞春末開拔的兵季慣例推得，並非史料記載。
dataEn: The chronology has to be set out first. Hammurabi's reign is conventionally given as 1792 to 1750 BC. Mari was destroyed by Hammurabi in 1760 BC, and the palace archive of Mari has been excavated by a French archaeological team since 1933, giving up tens of thousands of tablets. Shamshi-Adad I occupied Babylon around 1775 BC. The Hittite king Anitta levelled Hassuwa and Alalakh in the early seventeenth century; Hattusili I reigned roughly 1650 to 1620 BC, and the year in which his son Mursili I entered Babylon is conventionally given as 1595 BC. The 1740 BC used by the list comes out of the older chronology: working backwards from the succession of kings, on the reckoning of the Babylonian King List A, which converts the Kassite rule into a span of several centuries, the Kassite seizure of Babylon was fixed in the old account at 1740 BC, and scholarship had already shortened that series of dates by about a hundred and fifty years before the middle of the twentieth century. The 1740 and the 1700 in the same list therefore belong to the old chronology, while the 1595 belongs to the new one, and the two do not share an origin. On the scale of the city: Babylon in the Old Babylonian period covered less than a hundred hectares, the outer wall was raised under Sin-Muballit I and ran for kilometres around the town, and the temple quarter and the tablet archives within it run to tens of thousands of items. Between 1901 and 1902 Jacques de Morgan's excavations at Susa brought up the stele of the Code of Hammurabi; that stele had been carried out of Babylon in 1595 BC and is now in the Louvre in Paris, and it is the most concrete single piece of evidence this war has left. The length of the Kassite rule in Babylonia is given in the documents as four hundred and twenty-six years, and that dynasty ended around 1155 BC when the Elamite king Shutruk-Nahhunte sacked Babylon. The month entered here, April, is inferred from the normal spring opening of the Mesopotamian campaigning season and is not a documented date.
cause: 巴比倫帝國的衰弱並非一場入侵造成，而是三層原因同時發作。最表層是王朝的內部機制：漢摩拉比帝國是一個靠個人與宗族關係維繫的征服聯盟，君主一死，諸城與神廟就各自尋找出路；王位繼承本身就是宮廷政變，軍隊與王權分離，禁衛與雇傭兵只聽命於出錢的一方。往下一層是地理與資源：巴比倫的核心在幼發拉底河中游的沖積平原，木材、銅料、錫料都得靠商路輸入，北方高原的國家一旦壯大並控制商路，巴比倫的邊界就從一個地理事實變成一個爭議；它不能放棄北方，又沒有能力長期駐紮北方，於是每次遠征都把王國的存亡押在一次進攻上。最深的一層是軍事技術的變化：馬匹與輕型戰車帶來的不只是火力，而是機動與徵召方式的革命。從前城牆與灌溉渠可以把一個農業帝國綁在原地；有了車隊，任何結合了騎射與商隊網絡的武裝集團都可以脫離城牆、在河谷裡反覆打擊，而沒有馬匹的一方只能靠圍牆死守。於是阿摩利王朝的崩解與加喜特人的上升是同一件事的兩面：王朝先用帝國式遠征耗盡了自己，隨後被同樣學會了車戰與徵召的集團接管。赫梯的介入則是外部推力：哈圖西里一世與穆爾西里一世要的是幼發拉底河中游的商路與銅料，這與巴比倫的生存空間完全重疊。
causeEn: The weakening of the Babylonian empire was not produced by an invasion; three layers of cause operated at once. At the surface lay the internal mechanism of the dynasty. The empire of Hammurabi was a conquest league held together by personal and kinship ties, and once a king died the cities and the shrines each looked for their own way out; the succession to the throne was itself a palace coup, the army separated from the crown, and the guard and the mercenaries obeyed whoever paid them. One layer down lay geography and raw materials. The core of Babylon was the alluvial plain of the middle Euphrates, and timber, copper and tin all had to come in along the caravan roads; once a state of the northern highlands grew strong and closed the roads, the Babylonian frontier stopped being a geographical fact and became a matter of dispute. It could not abandon the north, and it could not garrison the north for long, so every expedition put the survival of the kingdom on a single offensive. The deepest layer was a change in military technology. The horse and the light chariot brought not so much firepower as a revolution in movement and in the raising of troops. Walls and irrigation canals had formerly been enough to pin an agrarian empire in place; once there were wagon teams, any armed group combining mounted archery with a caravan network could leave the walls, strike up and down the valley again and again, while the side without horses could only sit behind its walls. The collapse of the Amorite dynasty and the rise of the Kassites are thus two faces of the same thing: the dynasty first exhausted itself in imperial expeditions, and was then taken over by a group that had learned the same lessons of chariot warfare and of recruitment. The Hittite intervention was the external push: what Hattusili I and Mursili I wanted was the trade routes and the copper of the middle Euphrates, and that overlapped completely with the space in which Babylon had to live.
impact: 這段歷史的後果要分巴比倫與外面兩個方向來看。對巴比倫本身，第一是王朝斷裂而制度未斷：帝國的行政、度量衡與法律框架沒有隨王朝一起消失，而是被加喜特（卡西特）統治者原樣接手，書吏繼續用蘇美爾—阿卡德語書寫，泥板行政傳統沒有中斷；卡西特時期新出現的庫杜魯界石，把王室授予土地的過程做成可以公開查驗的法律文件，是兩河流域土地法最完整的一套實物，說明統治形式換了而制度仍在運作。第二是編年與檔案的黑暗：從巴比倫第一王朝末期到卡西特時期早段，兩河流域留下的文字材料明顯稀少，學者稱之為古巴比倫時期的黑暗時代，一段約兩百年的空隙；正是在這段空隙裡，巴比倫尼亞的政治記憶靠王表與界石維持，而《漢摩拉比法典》的真正名聲，要到二十世紀初石柱出土才重新回到世界。對外方面，這段戰爭把巴比倫的書寫傳統帶進了安納托利亞：巴比倫的泥板文獻被帶到哈圖沙，赫梯王宮的檔案裡出現了巴比倫的文學作品與埃蘭傳說，兩河流域的敘事傳統在安納托利亞落地生根。亞述則在巴比倫崩潰後接管了美索不達米亞，把阿卡德語世界的名分接過去，終於在公元前七世紀成為兩河唯一的強權。長期看，這段衰敗並沒有讓巴比倫消失：卡西特人給它留下了王朝的格式，亞述人給它留下了帝國的規模，直到公元前六世紀末新巴比倫王朝興起，直到居魯士入城，巴比倫這個王朝觀念仍被一再復原。
impactEn: The consequences of this stretch of history run in two directions, one looking into Babylonia and one looking out of it. For Babylonia itself, first, the dynasty broke while the institutions did not. The administrative machinery, the weights and measures and the legal framework of the empire did not disappear with the dynasty; they were taken over as they stood by the Kassite rulers, the scribes kept writing in Sumero-Akkadian, and the tradition of administration on clay was never interrupted. The kudurru boundary stones that first appear in the Kassite period turned the granting of land by the crown into a legal document that could be checked in public, and they are the most complete set of material evidence for land law in Mesopotamia; the form of rule changed while the machinery kept working. Second, there was a darkness in the record. From the end of the Babylonian First Dynasty into the early Kassite period the written material from Mesopotamia becomes markedly thin, and scholars call it the dark age of the Old Babylonian period, a gap of about two hundred years. It was in that gap that the political memory of Babylonia was kept alive by king lists and boundary stones, and the real fame of the Code of Hammurabi did not return to the world until the stele was unearthed in the twentieth century. Outwardly, this war carried the Babylonian writing tradition into Anatolia: Babylonian tablets were brought to Hattusa, and the palace archives there contain Babylonian literary works and Elamite tales, so that the narrative tradition of Mesopotamia took root in Anatolia. Assyria in the meantime took over Mesopotamia after Babylon's collapse, inherited the name of the Akkadian world, and in the seventh century BC became the single power of the two rivers. In the long run this decline did not make Babylon disappear. The Kassites left it the format of a dynasty, the Assyrians left it the scale of an empire, and until the Neo-Babylonian dynasty rose at the end of the sixth century BC, and until Cyrus entered the city, the idea of Babylon as a dynasty was restored again and again.
result: 這段衰落的終局寫在公元前1595年。穆爾西里一世率赫梯軍隊越過幼發拉底河，攻入巴比倫城，城市遭到洗劫，王室成員、祭司與神像被帶往安納托利亞的高地；漢摩拉比的法典石柱也在這一批戰利品中離開了巴比倫，一千三百多年後才在蘇薩出土。巴比倫城本身並未就此消失：它被降為地方行政中心，神廟與學校在隨後數百年間重新修復，泥板的傳統延續下來；真正被終止的是阿摩利王朝的統治形式，以及幼發拉底河中游霸權這個格局。城破之後，赫梯人並沒有佔有河谷的治理能力，這一課直接導致赫梯舊王國在安納托利亞的退縮，以及亞述在北方把勢力推回幼發拉底河。而加喜特（卡西特）人在巴比倫尼亞的統治，以文獻可考的四百二十六年計，約在公元前1155年告終：埃蘭王舒特魯克納胡恩特洗劫巴比倫，把馬爾杜克的神像帶回蘇薩，後來才被新巴比倫人贖回重立。把整段弧線拉回來看，列表所謂的巴比倫帝國的衰弱與滅亡，講的其實不是一個帝國被一次攻擊摧毀，而是一次結構性崩解：王朝的軍隊先後於農業、灌溉與商路之上重建，帝國形式先失血，接著城市被接管、被洗劫，而城市的名字、神廟與書寫傳統卻在別人手里延續了起來。
resultEn: The end of this decline is written in the year 1595 BC. Mursili I led the Hittite army across the Euphrates and into the city of Babylon, the town was plundered, and members of the royal house, priests and gods were carried off to the Anatolian highlands; the stele of Hammurabi's law left Babylon among that booty and was not unearthed at Susa until more than thirteen centuries later. The city of Babylon itself did not disappear: it was reduced to a provincial administrative centre, its shrines and its scribal schools were rebuilt over the following centuries, and the tradition of the clay tablet carried on. What was ended was the form of Amorite rule, and with it the pattern of Babylonian primacy in the middle Euphrates. After the fall of the city, the Hittites proved unable to govern the valley, and that lesson told directly on the withdrawal of the Old Hittite kingdom from Anatolia and on Assyria pushing power back down the Euphrates from the north. The rule of the Kassites in Babylonia, counting the four hundred and twenty-six years the documents give, ended around 1155 BC, when the Elamite king Shutruk-Nahhunte sacked Babylon and carried the image of Marduk back to Susa, to be redeemed and re-erected in the city by the Neo-Babylonians. Taking the whole arc together, what the list calls the decline and fall of the Babylonian empire is not the destruction of an empire by a single blow but a structural collapse. The armies of the dynasty were rebuilt on top of agriculture, irrigation and the caravan roads; the imperial form bled out first, and then the city was taken over and then sacked, while the name of the city, its shrines and its writing tradition went on in other people's hands.
